relations.evidence: Couchbase transactions enable you to carry out ACID (atomic, consistent, isolated, and durable) actions on the database. This how-to guide covers SQL++ support for Couchbase transactions. Some SDKs also support Couchbase transactions. For more information, see [Related Links](#related-links).

notable_absence.finding: As on the n1ql-reference transactions.json page, no privilege, role, or edition gate is named on this task-level guide either - the only hard constraint stated is an access-surface one (cbq shell required) and a data-safety warning (the examples mutate the sample dataset).

cross_component_finding: This round's central open question is answered directly by the page's own framing, not by inference: `transactions.md` (the guide) is explicitly and exclusively the SQL++-statement-level transaction model (n1ql:transactions/begin-transaction/commit-transaction/rollback-transaction/set-transaction/savepoint family from round 5) - 'This how-to guide covers SQL++ support for Couchbase transactions.' It is emphatically NOT the Java-SDK-level sdk:distributed-transaction concept from round 4; the SDK feature is acknowledged in exactly one sentence ('Some SDKs also support Couchbase transactions') plus a 'Transactions with SDKs' related-links list of 10 per-SDK distributed-acid-transactions-from-the-sdk pages, with zero SDK code samples inline on this guide page itself. The guide reuses the n1ql: statement family wholesale (BEGIN/SET/SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK/COMMIT TRANSACTION, tximplicit) and adds no new SQL++-level transaction concept - only task framing (transaction parameters via \SET, single- vs. multiple-statement transactions) around the pre-existing statements. This is the strongest single-file confirmation of the round's core hypothesis: guide content here is pure task-level repackaging of round 5's reference vocabulary, not a third framing.
cross_product_finding: The 'Query Transaction Simulator' (https://transactions.couchbase.com) and the 10-SDK 'Transactions with SDKs' related-links list are both new surface area not seen in round 5's n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/transactions.json (which linked only to a Couchbase blog post and the server/ transactions overview) - this guide is slightly richer in its cross-links to the SDK ecosystem than the reference page was, even though it still does not merge or conflate the SQL++ and SDK transaction models.
